39b289.evidence: Independently reproduced unauthenticated: GET /index.jsp?content=../WEB-INF/web.xml → HTTP 200, 14141 bytes, body embeds the real deployment descriptor (7380 bytes, <web-app>…</web-app>). Proved it is genuine file content, not a template/whitelist: `content=WEB-INF/web.xml` (no traversal) and `content=../WEB-INF/does-not-exist.xml` both return "not available"; a second protected file (../META-INF/MANIFEST.MF) is also readable. Encoded variants `..%2f`, `%2e%2e%2f`, `..%5c` all return the same descriptor. Deeper traversal (../../) NPEs (Tomcat clamps at webapp root), so the read is bounded to the deployed application. /default.jsp does not exist (404); the sink is /index.jsp only. Filed as vuln-0003 (High, CVSS 7.5, CWE-22).

history.evidence: CONFIRMED during recon: GET /index.jsp?content=../WEB-INF/web.xml returned the full 14141-byte web.xml (servlet/filter mappings). One `../` level works; deeper → 500. PoC is read-only. Formal report not yet filed — reporting agent should file it.

9ddcff.risk_area: Broken function level authorization / privilege escalation
9ddcff.evidence: RE-VALIDATED and REPORTED as vuln-0005 (High, CVSS 8.1). Independently reproduced: jsmith (non-admin — /bank/main.jsp renders no ADMINISTRATION link, role 'user') reaches /admin/admin.jsp (200) and invokes admin functions. Web servlet path performs REAL state changes: POST /admin/addUser creates a user that authenticates; POST /admin/changePassword resets a pre-existing non-owned account (test_normal_abc) to an attacker-chosen password and the attacker logs in as it; POST /admin/addAccount adds accounts (800026/800027). Root cause confirmed from leaked web.xml + public AltoroJ source: AdminFilter is mapped to the misspelled /adimn/* so it never runs; AdminServlet has no role check; AuthFilter only requires login. API /api/admin/* accepted jsmith's token (200) vs 401 without; note the API handlers gate the DB write on enableAdminFunctions=false so they currently no-op, but still lack any role enforcement. Earlier apparent no-op was due to both login paths lowercasing the password — controlled for.

history.evidence: CONFIRMED: regular user jsmith token (from POST /api/login) drives /api/admin/addUser and changePassword to HTTP 200 "success" (401 without token); created test user reconprobe1. Web /admin/admin.jsp reachable by jsmith (AuthFilter only; AdminFilter only on typo /adimn/*). Report pending.

3c3f4b.evidence: Independently reproduced as jsmith. GET /api/account consistently lists only 15 owned accounts (800002,800003,4539082039396288,800011,800013-800023); enumerating 800000-800030 returned full balance + credits/debits + last_10_transactions for 12 accounts NOT in that list (800000,800001,800004-800010,800012,800024,800025). Negative control: non-existent 800026-800030 -> 500 {Error:null}; 800999/transactions -> {"Error":null}, proving real distinct records. Source confirms AccountAPI.java:63 'not checking the account number'. Filed vuln-0004 (CWE-639, CVSS 6.5, AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/C:H). Card 4539082039396288 is jsmith's OWN account and excluded. Note: POST /api/account/{no}/transactions is correctly scoped (user.lookupAccount).

history.evidence: CONFIRMED: account 800001 (not in jsmith's list 800002-800023) returns full balance+transactions via /api/account/800001 and "Account History - 800001" via showAccount?listAccounts=800001; 800010 returns 79903 bytes. Report pending.

b10ce9.evidence: Independently reproduced and filed as vuln-0002 (Medium, CVSS 6.5, C:H). With a jsmith session, GET /admin/admin.jsp (HTTP 200, 29636-30336 bytes) renders user <option> values containing plaintext username:password:role, including the administrator credential pdata1admin:admin_hacked:admin. Validation: POST /doLogin uid=admin&passw=admin_hacked returns 302 to /bank/main.jsp (SUCCESS), while the documented default admin/admin is rejected (302 to login.jsp) — negative control proving the leaked value is the genuine non-default secret; the /api/login token base64-decodes to admin:admin_hacked. Schema/records also leaked (PEOPLE columns incl PASSWORD/TOTP_SECRET/ROLE; ACCOUNTS columns/balances; ACCOUNTS/PEOPLE/FEEDBACK/TRANSACTIONS + Derby SYS.* tables). Data confirmed live: newly created accounts appear in the list immediately. jsmith (non-admin) reaches the page; role boundary already broken by BFLA (separate finding).

history.evidence: CONFIRMED: page leaks user <option> values containing credentials (e.g. pdata2attadmin:P@ssw0rd123:user, pdata1admin:admin_hacked:admin) plus DB schema/rows (Derby SYS.* tables; PEOPLE columns PASSWORD, TOTP_SECRET). Report pending.

ddbca9.evidence: Deployed ServletUtil.searchArticles matches articles with Java String.contains(query) over the parsed DOM — no XPath expression is compiled or evaluated. Proven behaviourally: known substrings match (Mercury, Announces, AppScan, fire, Watchfire) whereas the XPath tautology `ZZZ' or '1'='1` returns the same "News title not found" as the false predicate `ZZZ' or '1'='2` and as a benign non-match; the quote/`] | //* | //*['` payloads produced no error and no result-set change. Named control: ServletUtil.searchArticles uses `title.contains(query)` (substring containment), so no XPath metacharacter is interpreted.

history.evidence: Input sink confirmed: GET /bank/queryxpath.jsp?content=queryxpath.jsp&query=<title> executes an XPath query ("Watchfire" returned a news title). Quote injection not yet proven exploitable — needs boolean/blind exploitation.

edd7bc.evidence: No server-side fetch exists. The sink is implemented in `WebContent/util/serverStatusCheckService.jsp` as a 4-line JSP that only string-interpolates `request.getParameter("HostName")` into a JSON literal and returns the hardcoded constant `"HostStatus": "OK"` — there is no HTTP client, URL, socket, or any outbound call in the JSP or anywhere in the codebase (grep for openConnection/HttpURLConnection/new URL/HttpClient/Socket found no fetch sink; the only `Runtime.exec` is the local `content` file-include in index.jsp). The "status check" is performed entirely client-side by JavaScript (`serverStatusCheck.html` uses browser `XMLHttpRequest`), which is not SSRF. Behaviorally confirmed: identical `"OK"` and no timing differential (~0.23-0.25s baseline) for valid internal (127.0.0.1), external, malformed, and empty values, and an interactsh OOB payload (`HostName=<unique>.oast.site`) produced NO DNS/HTTP callback. The reflection itself is a separate, real issue that was filed as a reflected XSS (vuln-0001).

history.evidence: Endpoint reflects HostName and returns static {"HostStatus":"OK"} for valid, invalid, and malformed hosts with no timing/response differential; blind SSRF not confirmed — needs OOB interactsh validation.

5d1335.evidence: SQL injection CONFIRMED and reported (vuln-0009): the unparameterized credential query in DBUtil.isValidUser (string-concatenated Statement) permits authentication bypass including the admin account via the password field on POST /api/login and POST /doLogin (boolean oracle `' OR '1'='1` vs `' OR '1'='2`, plus a Derby lexical-error leak). /search.jsp `query` is NOT SQL-injectable: ServletUtil.searchSite -> searchFiles performs no database query and searchFiles explicitly returns empty for this demo; the parameter is only reflected into the page (Search Results block), with no SQL parsing or error of any kind.

history.evidence: Injection sinks identified (query reflected; doLogin/API login reach DB) but not yet tested with payloads. Hand to a SQLi validation agent.

328b06.surface: Session management: JSESSIONID, AltoroAccounts cookie, API token, logout
328b06.evidence: API bearer token design confirmed weak and reported as its own finding: token = base64(base64(user):base64(pass):<8 rand bytes>), trailing signature NOT validated (empty/arbitrary accepted), plaintext password recoverable from the token and reusable on /doLogin, and GET /api/logout does not invalidate (replay still 200). AltoroAccounts cookie (unsigned, non-HttpOnly base64 of acct~name~balance) was tampered with modified balances and an HTML/script name; values were NOT reflected into any server-rendered page (main.jsp/showAccount use session data) -> no spoofing/XSS impact. Reported under vuln-0013.

history.evidence: AltoroAccounts cookie is base64 of account names/balances, unsigned and not HttpOnly; API token is deterministic base64 of creds + 8 rand bytes; logout.jsp + /api/logout may not invalidate. Tamper/forge/replay not yet tested.

0b8aae.evidence: robots.txt and sitemap.xml both return the generic 404 page (6821 bytes baseline). No robots disallow hints. Custom 404 is a styled Altoro page.

f11720.evidence: wafw00f identified no WAF (generic detection, 7 requests). Server header Apache-Coyote direct; no CDN/WAF fingerprints. Testing can proceed unthrottled.

52ec50.evidence: With a valid Bearer token, GET /api/feedback/1 returns HTTP 500 with a Tomcat error page. Extracted content: exception type java.lang.IndexOutOfBoundsException wrapped in javax.servlet.ServletException, Jersey internals (org.glassfish.jersey.servlet.WebComponent/ ServletContainer), and application class/method names with line numbers (com.ibm.security.appscan.altoromutual.util.ServletUtil.getFeedback(ServletUtil.java:234), ...api.FeedbackAPI.getFeedback(FeedbackAPI.java:81)), plus the banner Apache Tomcat/7.0.92. a02e2d.risk_area: Broken object-level authorization / unauthorized fund transfer
a02e2d.evidence: jsmith's Bearer token drove a transfer with fromAccount=800001 (NOT in jsmith's /api/account list) into jsmith's 800011: HTTP 200 success, 800001 debited $1.00 (1002626437453.38 -> 1002626437452.38). Web /bank/doTransfer rejects the same source ("Originating account is invalid"), proving the API omits the ownership check. Report filed.

a70bc4.risk_area: Input validation – negative amount reverses fund flow
a70bc4.evidence: API accepts negative transferAmount and reverses debit/credit: from=own 800011 to victim 800001, amt=-1 -> 800011 +$1.00 (-0.01->0.99), 800001 -$1.00. Web endpoint rejects negative ("Transfer amount is invalid"). Also no insufficient-funds/upper-bound check (1,000,000 from a $342 balance succeeded; 1e30 accepted). Report filed.

3a6f9b.evidence: Self-transfer (from==to) is accepted despite client-side JS block; balance increases by the full amount with no debit. Web 3x $100 on 800023: 15->115->215->315. API $50 on 800023: 322->372. Confirmed on both endpoints. Report filed.

b3e938.risk_area: Race condition / lost update on balance
b3e938.evidence: 30 sequential $1 transfers 800013->800019 applied exactly (-30/+30); 30 concurrent identical transfers all returned HTTP 200 but moved only ~2-4 (src -2, dst +3). Non-atomic read-modify-write confirmed. Report filed.

a38b44.evidence: Named control at a specific location: FeedbackServlet.doPost (src/com/ibm/security/appscan/altoromutual/servlet/FeedbackServlet.java:47-67) reads ONLY name, email_addr, subject, comments - it never calls request.getParameter("cfile"). Feedback is persisted via OperationsUtil.sendFeedback -> DBUtil.storeFeedback (SQL INSERT INTO FEEDBACK, DBUtil.java:520-529); no path/file-write sink exists on this route. `cfile` occurs solely as a dead hidden input in WebContent/feedback.jsp:50 (grep over src/ and WebContent/ returns no other reference). No multipart/upload handling anywhere (no @MultipartConfig / getPart / ServletFileUpload / FileOutputStream in JSPs or servlets). Live confirmation on http://demo.testfire.net: 11 distinct cfile values (comments.txt, probe_up.txt, ../WebContent/..., ../WEB-INF/..., ../../..., /tmp/..., probe_up.jsp variants) all produced a byte-identical 200 "Thank You" (7029 bytes); the unique marker was unreadable at /probe_up.txt, /probe_up.jsp, /comments.txt (404) and via /index.jsp?content=../<file> traversal. Prior "needs_follow_up" was an artifact of testing a parameter the server ignores. NOT arbitrary file write.

history.evidence: POST returns 200 "Thank You" for any cfile value (comments.txt, plain, ../WEB-INF/x.jsp, ../../x, /tmp/x) but the written content (unique marker) could not be read back at /index.jsp?content=../<file>, /<file>, or any tested path. Write not proven.

8997c6.risk_area: Input validation – negative amount on web endpoint
8997c6.evidence: Web TransferServlet rejects negatives: POST with transferAmount=-25 returned "ERROR: Transfer amount is invalid" and balances were unchanged. Control runs before any balance update.

34a3de.evidence: Specific control: CCApplyServlet (src/com/ibm/security/appscan/altoromutual/servlet/CCApplyServlet.java) reads exactly ONE request parameter, `passwd` (line 47); it binds no other field, stores nothing and changes no account/credit state ("do nothing with credit card application"). Field injection / mass assignment is therefore impossible — any role/balance/approval-style parameter is silently ignored. Verified live with a jsmith session: GET /bank/ccApply -> 405 (POST-only, explains the earlier GET 405); POST with no passwd -> 500 (NPE at passwd.trim(), explains the earlier generic-POST 500); POST passwd=demo1234 -> 200 /bank/applysuccess.jsp ("Your new Altoro Mutual Gold VISA"); POST passwd=wrong -> 200 /bank/apply.jsp ("Login Failed..."). The only sink is passwd -> DBUtil.isValidUser(username, passwd.trim().toLowerCase()), the unparameterized credential query already reported as vuln-0009. Even a successful injection there merely yields applysuccess.jsp with no state change, so it does not constitute unauthorized field binding or business-logic abuse and is not separately reportable.

history.evidence: GET -> 405 (POST-only). POST with generic fields -> HTTP 500; form field set not mapped and no field-driven logic impact observed. Could not confirm a parameter-tampering issue.

b4283c.evidence: step accepts 1/2/99/a and only selects a static template (200, ~7000B, no state change, no error); /static/doSurvey GET returns a static 272B stub and POST -> 405. No server-side state machine to abuse.

5f19c3.evidence: Specific control: the `enableFeedbackRetention` app property is false on the deployed instance, and every feedback write/render path is gated on it. Proven by the write oracle — POST /api/feedback/submit returns the JSON echo branch {name,email,subject,comments} and NOT the {"status":"Thank you!","feedbackId":...} branch, which per OperationsUtil.sendFeedback (OperationsUtil.java:122) is only produced when the property is true; with it false sendFeedback returns null and DBUtil.storeFeedback is never called, so the FEEDBACK table is never written. The only consumers of that table are two property-gated render blocks — feedbacksuccess.jsp:51 (renders the submitted row) and admin/feedbackReview.jsp:33 (renders ALL rows) — and both skip their block: POST /sendFeedback -> feedbacksuccess.jsp (200) contains no "Details of your feedback submission" and no "Your Name:"; GET /admin/feedbackReview.jsp (200, reachable) contains no "Customer feedback submissions" heading and zero "Feedback ID:" rows. No other JSP/HTML page renders stored feedback (grep: only feedbacksuccess.jsp, admin/feedbackReview.jsp and the property-gated membertoc.jspf link reference it). With the property off there is no stored feedback to render anywhere, so no stored-XSS sink is reachable. (The earlier "feedback was stored" observation was incorrect — the API oracle shows the write branch was not taken.)

No HTML view rendering stored feedback was found (probed /feedback.txt, /comments.txt, /admin/feedback.jsp, /bank/feedback.jsp — 404/302; admin.jsp does not render feedback rows).
